name: Amoxicillin
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Amoxicillin is mainly excreted unchanged in urine (about 60% of an oral dose in 6 to 8 hours). The US label needs no dose change unless kidney impairment is severe: below a GFR of 30 mL/min do not use the 875 mg dose, give 250 or 500 mg every 12 hours (GFR 10–30) or every 24 hours (below 10), and give extra doses during and after hemodialysis.
kidney_function_basis: Label states GFR in mL/min (not indexed); cut-offs 30 and 10. Shown in the CrCl band rows.

bands.recommendation: No dose change; the label reduces dose only below GFR 30 (label).
GFR 10–30: 500 mg or 250 mg every 12 hours by severity; do not use the 875 mg dose (label).
GFR 10–14: 500 mg or 250 mg every 12 hours. GFR below 10: 500 mg or 250 mg every 24 hours by severity. No 875 mg dose (label).

hd.text: 500 mg or 250 mg every 24 hours by severity, plus an additional dose both during and at the end of dialysis (label).

pd.text: No peritoneal dialysis dosing in label. For PD-associated peritonitis (ISPD 2022): continuous intraperitoneal maintenance dose 150 mg/L in each exchange; no intermittent data. Specialist input.

crrt.text: Not in label; the cited CRRT review (Li 2020) gives no regimen for this drug. Specialist input.
crrt.short: No CRRT data in cited sources

dialyzable: Yes: may be removed by hemodialysis (label). About 20% protein bound.
monitoring: Kidney function for dose; rash; diarrhea (CDAD); INR with oral anticoagulants (label). Crystalluria and interstitial nephritis reported after overdose; keep fluid intake up.

pediatric.usual_dose: 12 weeks (3 months) or younger: up to 30 mg/kg/day divided every 12 hours (immature kidney function) (label 2.3). Over 3 months: 20 to 45 mg/kg/day divided every 8 to 12 hours, by infection and severity; 40 kg or more: adult dose (label).

renal.recommendation: No dosing recommendations for children with kidney impairment (label). Specialist input.
